original_value: The objective of the work is to explore the potency of integrating structural and citation information with effective syntax‐semantic text‐based analysis for scientific plagiarism detection. One of the major limitations in today's plagiarism checkers is their sole dependence on text‐based detection, where they ignore the citation and structural information. Further, the text‐based detection approaches that they employ usually fail to trace out intelligent manipulations. In the proposed work, a plagiarism detection system is presented that employs the effective coupling of various modules, namely, logical structure classifications and citation parsing, two‐stage candidate document selections, syntax‐semantic‐based exhaustive passage level analysis with plagiarism analysis using structural and citation information. Further, a new plagiarism score, namely, weighted overall similarity index is proposed, opposed to the general plagiarism scores. The proposed approach is evaluated on the data set created by Alzahrani et al. (), which contains scientific publications imposed with various plagiarism complexities. Comparison of the final system results is done against a potential baseline approach. The proposed approach exhibits considerable improvement over the comparative baseline, and hence reflects the potency of syntax‐semantic text‐based analysis with structural and citation information.

result.paraphrase: The work aims to investigate how combining structural and citation information with effective syntax-semantic text-based analysis can improve scientific plagiarism detection. A key weakness of current plagiarism checkers is their exclusive reliance on text-based detection, which overlooks citation and structural cues. In addition, the text-based methods they use generally cannot uncover intelligent manipulations. The proposed plagiarism detection system integrates several modules, including logical structure classification, citation parsing, two-stage candidate document selection, and exhaustive passage-level syntax-semantic analysis that incorporates structural and citation information. It also introduces a new plagiarism metric, the weighted overall similarity index, rather than conventional plagiarism scores. The approach is evaluated on the dataset created by Alzahrani et al. (), which includes scientific publications with varying levels of plagiarism complexity. The final system results are compared with a strong baseline approach. The proposed method shows substantial improvement over the comparative baseline, demonstrating the effectiveness of syntax-semantic text-based analysis together with structural and citation information.
